definition: Transmute means to change one substance or form into another.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word transmute. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know transmute should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the cellar's crocks, salt and time transmute shredded cabbage into sauerkraut, a food the raw leaf only hints at.
Convert is milder than transmute — a converted barn is still the same timber put to new use, while transmuted matter has become a different substance altogether.
Transfigure goes further than transmute — transmuting changes what a thing is made of, but transfiguring lifts its whole appearance into something radiant and scarcely recognizable.

To transform is to remake something so dramatically that it reads as new — the renovated warehouse, the actor unrecognizable in costume. The change announces itself. Transmute is quieter and deeper at once: it claims the very material has crossed over into a different substance, whatever the surface shows.

To recast is to pour the same material into a new shape or role — a lecture recast as an essay, a myth recast for the stage. The material survives the move; only its form is new. Transmute changes the material itself: lead into gold, grief into music.
